provenance.notes: A length-64 window over 4,159 samples with frame step one produces 4,096 frames of 33 one-sided frequency bins.
A 4,096-frame, 64-point transform with `onesided=0` requires the full spectrum and exercises the shared twiddle-table FFT.
A real 512-point STFT over 4,097 transforms exercises packed processing and leaves one partial four-transform workgroup when that specialization is available.

skipGpu.reason: Portable WGSL floating-point semantics do not guarantee preservation of the subnormal values required by this fixture. Backend evidence: Metal FTZ: subnormal 1e-40 impulse flushes to zero on GPU, every one-sided bin reads 0 instead of the subnormal value (tolerance 0).

provenance.notes: Focused amplitude edge: a one-frame rectangular STFT of a subnormal impulse should preserve that value in every real one-sided bin.
Compact scalar-frame-step projection of ORT's windowed STFT test.
Official rectangular-window fixture: window is omitted and frame_length supplies the DFT size.
Two-sided projection of ORT's constant-window STFT setup; validates the full spectrum instead of the default one-sided bins.
Covers the ONNX optional-input form where frame_length is provided and the window input is omitted.
A two-batch, complex-valued signal STFT without a window input, adapted from ONNX Runtime's two-sided complex-input test.
Batched complex STFT without an explicit window uses frame_length as the rectangular-window length.
A two-batch, complex-valued signal STFT with a constant window of length 4, adapted from ONNX Runtime's frame-offset complex-input test.
A real length-512 transform with onesided=0 emits the full 512-bin spectrum; frame step 256 produces three frames.
A 4,096-point one-sided STFT with a window checks the real-frequency output across the full transform length.

A 2048-point window exercises the in-place radix-2 specialization at the 16 KiB WebGPU workgroup-storage minimum: its 8 bytes per element scratch fits while the 16 bytes per element two-buffer scratch does not. On larger storage limits the case remains valid and may use the two-buffer specialization instead, so it requires no explicit device limit.
A 4,096-point complex STFT checks the full-spectrum output and frequency-bin order.
Real onesided 400-point mixed-radix path: 16-point shared Stockham transforms over 25 residue classes, followed by the direct radix-25 tail.
Generic mixed-radix recurrence with a 32-point shared Stockham factor and radix-9 tail.
Complex/full-spectrum branch of the 16x25 mixed-radix decomposition.
Real full-spectrum 480-point mixed-radix path: 32-point shared Stockham transforms over 15 residue classes, followed by the direct radix-15 tail.
Generic mixed-radix recurrence at the supported tail bound: a 16-point shared Stockham factor and radix-31 tail.
First tail past the unanchored bound: a 4-point shared Stockham factor and radix-33 tail, so the tail walk re-anchors exactly once.
Window length 1,000 factors as 8 x 125, selecting the shared mixed-radix transform. With onesided=0, each frame emits the full 1,000-bin spectrum.
The final four samples cannot fill an eight-sample frame, so ONNX floor framing emits only the complete frame at offset zero.
The frame at offset four would extend past the six-sample signal, so ONNX floor framing emits only the complete frame at offset zero.
The first non-power-of-two window above 512 checks real STFT output. Three frames exercise frame addressing; 257 bins exercise the partial second 256-frequency block.
A real STFT with a window length other than 513 checks partial frequency tiles.
A large radix-2 FFT with length other than 4096 checks complete frequency output across device tiers.
A length-512 one-sided transform with fixed window and signal values exposes twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.
A length-512 one-sided transform with fixed window and signal values exposes twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.
A length-480 one-sided transform (not a power of two) with fixed window and signal values exposes twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.
A length-400 one-sided transform (not a power of two) with fixed window and signal values exposes twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.

A length-1000 transform with onesided explicitly set to 0 returns the full 1000-point spectrum; fixed window and signal values expose twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.

A length-513 one-sided transform, one sample past the 512 power-of-two length, checks non-power-of-two handling; fixed window and signal values expose twiddle and accumulation error under a strict comparison tolerance.
